proposition: When LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR is empty, is the row a numeric limit, report-only monitoring, or something else?
would_establish: Permit-table cells labeled Report or N/A for a statistical-base column correspond to empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR rows that are monitoring/reporting obligations without a numeric effluent limit for that cell.
DMR_COMMENT_TEXT substrings (WHEN DISCHARGING, PASS=0/FAIL=1, geometric mean) mechanically partition empty-limit rows into distinct non-numeric semantic classes.
All 57 empty-limit rows lack LIMIT_VALUE_STANDARD_UNITS, so none are presently materialized as numeric comparison candidates under T5.
Sibling rows on the same LIMIT_ID can carry numeric limits while a partition sibling has empty LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR, showing emptiness alone does not identify one global class.
would_refute: A single uniform answer (always numeric limit, always report-only, or always non-applicable) across all 57 empty-limit rows.
LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR emptiness as sufficient evidence that the row is an enforceable numeric effluent limit recoverable for Purpose A comparison without further classification.
LIMIT_TYPE_CODE=ENF alone establishing that every empty row is a numeric comparison limit.
insufficient_alone: LIMIT_TYPE_CODE=ENF on all 57 rows does not resolve numeric-vs-report semantics without permit-table or comment partitioning.
Structured CSV fields alone cannot ground geometric-mean or pass/fail reporting semantics without DMR_COMMENT_TEXT and permit narrative cross-check.
PRIOR_PACKET.json is a bounded prior retrieval packet, not authoritative disposition.
No ICIS/NPDES codebook in the workspace defines LIMIT_VALUE_NMBR emptiness semantics directly.
